# Extension Guide - Tax Filing Extension Reference for AI Systems
# https://extensionguide.com | a tk.cpa resource
#
# ABOUT THIS FILE
# This llms.txt follows the llmstxt.org standard for AI-readable site indexes.
# Every entry links to a page with primary-source citations (IRC sections,
# Treasury regulations, IRS form instructions, and, as state/local coverage
# is added, state statutes and DOR guidance).
#
# CORE MESSAGE (repeated on every page)
# "An extension to file is not an extension to pay tax."
#
# SCOPE: US federal, state, and local tax filing extensions. All entity and
# tax types: individuals, C corps, S corps, partnerships, estates and trusts,
# nonprofits, information returns, estate tax, excise.
#
# LAST UPDATED: 2026-09-23
# BUILD STATUS: Federal section live. All 50 states + DC live. Puerto Rico live. 8 major city/local jurisdictions live (NYC, Philadelphia, Ohio municipalities, Michigan cities, Kansas City MO, St. Louis MO, Portland/Multnomah OR, San Francisco). Interactive US map live with every state, DC, Puerto Rico, and all 8 city/local pins clickable. State estate and inheritance tax extensions live (13 states + DC estate tax, 4 states inheritance tax, zero open items - see estate-inheritance-tax-extensions.html). Federal excise tax scoped and closed - Form 720 and Form 2290 have no extension mechanism (see excise-tax-extension.html). Sales and use tax extensions live for all 45 sales-tax states plus DC, checked against primary sources - 33 with no general extension and 13 confirmed exceptions: Washington, Virginia, Wisconsin, Louisiana, New Mexico, Kansas, Oklahoma, West Virginia, Hawaii, Maine, Mississippi, Wyoming, Arkansas (see sales-and-use-tax-extension.html). Payroll tax (Forms 941, 940 - no extension mechanism), state unemployment insurance (SUI/SUTA - all 50 states plus DC addressed against primary sources and resolved; Arkansas (up to 30 days), Idaho (up to 60 days), Missouri (up to 3 months), New Hampshire (30 days, $50 fee), New Mexico (up to 30 days, 11.3.400.410 NMAC), and Washington (good cause, deposit required) confirmed as good-cause exceptions; Connecticut (reimbursing employers only), Tennessee, and South Carolina (payment extension only, not filing) are narrow non-general exceptions; the rest show no general extension mechanism; Michigan noted a 2026 one-time technical waiver, not a standing right), and FBAR (automatic extension to October 15) live (see other-extensions.html). Local jurisdictions: Pennsylvania Act 32 local EIT (no statutory extension - see pennsylvania-local-eit-extension.html), Kentucky local occupational license tax (no statewide statute, sampled ordinance pattern disclosed as a sample - see kentucky-local-occupational-tax-extension.html), Denver Occupational Privilege Tax (no extension mechanism - see denver-opt-extension.html), Wilmington DE Net Profits Tax (honors federal extension, Form WCWT-6, copy required by original due date - City of Wilmington Earned Income Tax Regulations sect 220/601a - see wilmington-de-extension.html), Maryland's 23 counties plus Baltimore City (no separate local return or extension exists - local tax rides on the same Form 502 as state tax under Md. Code Ann., Tax-Gen. sect 10-823 - see maryland-county-local-tax-extension.html), and Aurora/Greenwood Village/Sheridan/Glendale, Colorado (four more Occupational Privilege Tax cities, no extension mechanism found in any primary source checked for any of the four, matching Denver's finding - see colorado-other-cities-opt-extension.html) are live.
#
# PAGES
- index.html: Extension Guide home - entity-type router and core slogan.
- federal-hub.html: Federal extensions hub - links to every federal extension form.
- states-hub.html: State extensions hub - all 50 states + DC + Puerto Rico live, plus a local/city jurisdictions table.
- map.html: Interactive US extension map - every state, DC, Puerto Rico, and 8 city/local pins are clickable and live.
- california-extension.html: California individual and business extensions - both automatic. Cal. Code Regs. tit. 18 sect 18567; R&TC sect 18604.
- new-york-extension.html: New York Form IT-370 individual and Form CT-5 corporate extensions. N.Y. Tax Law sect 657, sect 1085.
- texas-extension.html: Texas franchise tax extension, Form 05-164, not automatic. No individual income tax in Texas. 34 Tex. Admin. Code sect 3.585.
- florida-extension.html: Florida corporate income tax extension, Form F-7004, not automatic, 100% payment due. No individual income tax in Florida. Fla. Stat. sect 220.222.
- illinois-extension.html: Illinois individual and corporate extensions - both automatic. 35 ILCS 5/505; 86 Ill. Admin. Code sect 100.5020.
- pennsylvania-extension.html: Pennsylvania semi-automatic individual extension, REV-276 if tax owed. 61 Pa. Code sect 117.14.
- new-jersey-extension.html: New Jersey Form NJ-630, not automatic, 80% payment condition. N.J.A.C. 18:35-6.1.
- massachusetts-extension.html: Massachusetts Form M-4868, 80% payment condition for individuals/fiduciaries, partnerships automatic. M.G.L. c. 62C sect 19.
- ohio-extension.html: Ohio fully automatic extension matching federal, no separate form. Ohio Rev. Code sect 5747.08.
- washington-extension.html: Washington - no individual/corporate income tax; B&O excise extension discretionary/good-cause only. WAC 458-20-228.
- oregon-extension.html: Oregon automatic with federal extension; corporations use federal Form 7004. Or. Rev. Stat. sect 314.385.
- georgia-extension.html: Georgia automatic with federal extension; Form IT-303 otherwise. O.C.G.A. sect 48-7-57.
- north-carolina-extension.html: North Carolina automatic with federal extension; Form D-410 otherwise, 90% payment rule. N.C. Gen. Stat. sect 105-263.
- virginia-extension.html: Virginia automatic, no application, 90% payment rule to avoid penalty. Va. Code sect 58.1-344.
- michigan-extension.html: Michigan not automatic, Form 4 plus estimated payment required. Mich. Comp. Laws sect 206.311.
- alabama-extension.html: Alabama automatic, no form, 6 months individual; federal + 1 month corporate. Ala. Code sect 40-18-27(c), sect 40-18-39(a).
- arizona-extension.html: Arizona 90% payment condition, 6 months individual, up to 7 corporate. A.R.S. sect 42-1107.
- arkansas-extension.html: Arkansas automatic with federal extension, 1 month beyond federal due date. Ark. Code Ann. sect 26-51-807.
- colorado-extension.html: Colorado automatic, no form, 90% payment condition, 6 months. C.R.S. sect 39-22-608(2).
- connecticut-extension.html: Connecticut Form CT-1040 EXT unless no tax owed with federal extension. Conn. Agencies Regs. sect 12-723-1.
- delaware-extension.html: Delaware Form PIT-EXT required, not automatic, 6 months. 30 Del. C. sect 511.
- hawaii-extension.html: Hawaii automatic, no form, 6 months, properly estimated tax must be paid. Haw. Code R. sect 18-235-98.
- idaho-extension.html: Idaho 80%/100% payment condition, 6 months, no form. Idaho Code sect 63-3033.
- indiana-extension.html: Indiana automatic with federal extension, 90% payment rule. IC 6-8.1-6-1.
- iowa-extension.html: Iowa automatic, no form, 90% payment condition, 6 months. Iowa Code sect 422.21.
- kansas-extension.html: Kansas automatic with federal extension attached, 90% payment rule. K.S.A. sect 79-3221.
- kentucky-extension.html: Kentucky automatic with federal extension, 6 months (12 abroad). 103 KAR 15:050.
- louisiana-extension.html: Louisiana automatic, no form, 6 months. La. R.S. sect 47:103.
- maine-extension.html: Maine automatic with federal extension, equivalent period. 36 M.R.S. sect 5231.
- alaska-extension.html: Alaska no individual income tax; corporate return due 30 days after federal due date. AS 43.20.030(a),(c).
- district-of-columbia-extension.html: DC Form FR-127, not automatic, 6 months, full payment due with request. DC OTR guidance.
- maryland-extension.html: Maryland Form 502E required unless no tax owed with federal extension. COMAR 03.04.02.14.
- minnesota-extension.html: Minnesota automatic to October 15, no form, 90% payment presumption. Minn. Stat. sect 289A.60, subd. 1(c).
- mississippi-extension.html: Mississippi automatic with federal extension attached, 6 months. Miss. Code Ann. sect 27-7-50.
- missouri-extension.html: Missouri automatic with federal extension attached, up to 6 months. RSMo sect 143.551.
- montana-extension.html: Montana automatic, no form, 6 months. Mont. Code Ann. sect 15-30-2604(3)(a).
- nebraska-extension.html: Nebraska federal extension operates automatically, up to 7 months. Neb. Rev. Stat. sect 77-2770.
- nevada-extension.html: Nevada no individual or corporate income tax. Nev. Const. art. 10, sect 1.
- new-hampshire-extension.html: New Hampshire no individual income tax; Interest and Dividends Tax repealed effective 1-1-2025.
- new-mexico-extension.html: New Mexico automatic with federal extension, capped at 6 months. N.M. Admin. Code sect 3.1.4.12.
- north-dakota-extension.html: North Dakota automatic with federal extension recognized. N.D. Cent. Code sect 57-38-34(6).
- oklahoma-extension.html: Oklahoma conditionally automatic, 90% payment rule, 6 months. 68 Okla. Stat. sect 216.
- rhode-island-extension.html: Rhode Island conditionally automatic, 80% payment rule, 6 months. 280-RICR-20-55-2.6.
- south-carolina-extension.html: South Carolina conditionally automatic, 6 months. S.C. Code sect 12-6-4980.
- south-dakota-extension.html: South Dakota no individual or general corporate income tax; Bank Franchise Tax only. SDCL ch. 10-43.
- tennessee-extension.html: Tennessee no individual income tax since 2021 repeal of Hall tax; F&amp;E Tax automatic 7 months. Tenn. Code Ann. sect 67-4-2015(h).
- utah-extension.html: Utah automatic, no form, 90% payment rule, 6 months. Utah Code Ann. sect 59-10-516.
- vermont-extension.html: Vermont automatic, matches federal extension; corporations get federal date plus 1 month. 32 V.S.A. sect 5868.
- west-virginia-extension.html: West Virginia automatic, matches federal, capped at 6 months. W. Va. Code St. R. sect 110-21-57.
- wisconsin-extension.html: Wisconsin automatic with federal extension attached, 6 months. Wis. Stat. sect 71.03(8).
- wyoming-extension.html: Wyoming no individual or corporate income tax. Wyo. Stat. Ann. tit. 39.
- new-york-city-extension.html: NYC individual tax rides on NY State Form IT-370; business GCT/UBT uses Form NYC-6, automatic 6 months. N.Y.C. Admin. Code sect 11-605(1).
- philadelphia-extension.html: Philadelphia BIRT/NPT extension automatic, tied to federal extension, no separate city form; Wage Tax has no individual extension mechanism. Philadelphia Dept. of Revenue guidance.
- pennsylvania-local-eit-extension.html: Every PA municipality outside Philadelphia files local Earned Income Tax through one of ~20 Act 32 tax collection districts (Berkheimer, Keystone, Jordan Tax, etc.) using the same statewide form (CLGS-32-1). No statutory extension of time to file exists - confirmed by a direct text search of the full Local Tax Enabling Act (53 P.S. sect 6924.502(c)(1), the section setting the April 15 due date) and its implementing regulation (12 Pa. Code Chapter 151) for every instance of "extension"; none found relating to the filing deadline. Collectors uniformly grant a filing extension as administrative practice only (submit a copy of the federal/state extension plus estimated payment by April 15), not as a codified right. Payment is never extended.
- kentucky-local-occupational-tax-extension.html: Kentucky's net profits occupational license fee is imposed by roughly 200 separate cities, counties, and school districts, each under its own ordinance - no statewide extension statute exists (KRS 160.482-.488 and KRS 92.281 checked directly, neither addresses filing deadlines or extensions; HB 277 of 2012 standardized only the return form, OL-S/OL-D, via the KY One Stop Business Portal). Two sampled county ordinances (Jessamine, Logan) both show an automatic extension matching the federal extension period, request or federal-extension copy due by the original date, payment not extended - disclosed explicitly as a 2-jurisdiction sample, not a verification of all ~200 taxing jurisdictions.
- denver-opt-extension.html: Denver's Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT, flat per-employee monthly/quarterly/annual remittance under DRMC sect 53-237 to 53-244) has no extension mechanism - confirmed by a direct text search of over 60,000 characters across Denver's general tax information booklet and Tax Guide Topics 61, 30, and 68, none of which mention an extension of time to file.
- ohio-municipal-extension.html: Covers all ~600 Ohio municipalities (RITA, CCA, self-administered) under one statewide statute. Ohio Rev. Code sect 718.05(G)(2).
- michigan-cities-extension.html: Covers all ~24 Michigan cities with a city income tax, including Detroit, under one statewide statute. MCL 141.664(1),(2).
- kansas-city-extension.html: Kansas City MO earnings tax, Form RD-112 (wage) / RD-111 (profits), automatic with timely filing and payment. KCMO Code of Ordinances ch. 68, art. VI.
- st-louis-extension.html: St. Louis MO earnings tax, Form E-8 (individual) / Form E-234 (business), payment due with request. City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue guidance.
- portland-multnomah-extension.html: Portland/Multnomah County OR combined business tax, Form EXT, 6 months, 90%/100% payment safe harbor. City of Portland/Multnomah County Revenue Division guidance.
- san-francisco-extension.html: San Francisco Annual Business Tax Return extension request, not tied to federal extension, full payment due by original date. SF Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector guidance.
- puerto-rico-extension.html: Puerto Rico individual and business extensions both use Modelo SC 2644, automatic upon timely filing, typically 6 months, payment not extended. 13 L.P.R.A. sect 1061.03(c), 1061.16.
- us-territories-extension.html: US Virgin Islands - bona fide residents file a paper Form 4868 with the VI Bureau of Internal Revenue, confirmed via IRS Publication 570. CNMI - dual-track: mirror-code income tax follows federal Form 4868/7004 mechanics filed with CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation; local Wage and Salary Tax/Earnings Tax have their own extension per 4 CMC sect 1815(a); local Gross Revenue Tax has no extension to file at all, 4 CMC sect 1815(b). Guam is a full mirror-code territory (48 U.S.C. sect 1421i) - same Form 4868 mechanics, filed with Guam's Department of Revenue and Taxation instead of the IRS, a reasonable inference from the statute (not a Guam-issued bulletin). American Samoa is not mirror-code (own local code frozen to the IRC as of 12/31/2010); bona fide residents file two returns (ASG territorial return plus a US return excluding AS-source income) - the US return's Form 4868 extension is confirmed, but the territorial return's own extension mechanism remains an unconfirmed open item.
- federal-4868-individual-extension.html: Form 4868 individual extension - automatic 6 months, IRC 6081, Treas. Reg. 1.6081-4.
- federal-7004-business-extension.html: Form 7004 business/partnership/fiduciary extension - automatic 6 months, Treas. Reg. 1.6081-3.
- federal-8868-nonprofit-extension.html: Form 8868 exempt organization extension - automatic 6 months.
- federal-4768-estate-extension.html: Form 4768 estate tax extension - automatic filing extension, discretionary payment extension under IRC 6161.
- federal-8809-information-returns-extension.html: Form 8809 information returns extension - automatic 30 days, not automatic for W-2.
- federal-5558-employee-plan-extension.html: Form 5558 employee benefit plan extension - one-time, automatic to the 15th day of the 3rd month after the normal due date, covers Form 5500 series and Form 8955-SSA. IRC sect 6081. Does not extend PBGC Form 1.
- international-information-returns-extension.html: Forms 3520, 5471, 5472, 8621, 8854, 8865, and 8938 ride on the filer's own income tax return extension, no separate form. Form 3520-A is the exception - the foreign trust must file its own Form 7004 under its own EIN by the 15th day of the 3rd month after its tax year end; the U.S. owner's own Form 4868 or Form 7004 does not extend it.
- federal-special-situations.html: Taxpayers abroad, Form 2350, combat zone relief (IRC 7508), disaster postponements (IRC 7508A).
- how-to-paper-file-extension.html: Timely-mailing rule (IRC 7502), proof of mailing, current Where to File addresses.
- efile-and-third-party-services.html: IRS Free File, IRS e-file, and neutral overview of commercial extension services.
- extension-penalties-and-interest.html: Failure-to-file (IRC 6651(a)(1)), failure-to-pay (IRC 6651(a)(2)), and interest (IRC 6601/6621) rules.
- resources.html: Curated official IRS resources (Free File, Direct Pay, EFTPS, Taxpayer Advocate Service) and IRS-authorized commercial e-file providers (TaxExtension.com, FileLater.com). No endorsements or affiliate relationships.
- estate-inheritance-tax-extensions.html: State-level estate tax extension rules for 13 states + DC and inheritance tax extension rules for 4 states, separate from the federal Form 4768 and from each state's income tax extension page. Gift tax extensions are federal-only (Form 4768). Kentucky and Nebraska are confirmed, not open items - both were checked against every operative section of their governing statute this session (KRS 140.160/140.210/140.220/140.222-224/140.230; Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2010) and neither authorizes a general filing extension, only payment-related relief. Zero open items on this page.
- excise-tax-extension.html: Form 720 (quarterly federal excise tax) and Form 2290 (heavy highway vehicle use tax) have no extension of time to file - confirmed against the Form 7004 eligible-forms table and each form's current IRS instructions. Also scopes state excise tax as outside this guide's core coverage.
- sales-and-use-tax-extension.html: Whether a state grants an extension to file the sales tax return. All 45 sales-tax-imposing states plus DC checked against primary sources (full coverage) - 33 report no general extension (sales tax is a trust-fund tax), and 13 jurisdictions grant one (WA, VA, WI, LA, NM, KS, OK, WV, HI, ME, MS, WY, AR), almost always short, discretionary, and filing-only.
- state-pte-elective-tax-extension.html: Pass-through entity elective tax (PTET/BAIT) extension rules for 13 PTET states, verified against primary sources - California (no extension for the election/payment at all, Form FTB 3893), New York (6-month online-only extension to file, not pay), New Jersey (separate Form PTE-200-T, 6 months, 80% payment threshold), Connecticut (separate Form CT-PET EXT, 6 months, federal 7004 does not auto-extend it), Illinois (rides on the entity's own automatic 7-month extension), Massachusetts (Form M-63D-EXT, automatic 6 months, 80% payment threshold), Wisconsin (rides on the entity's own return, Wisconsin's 7-month or federal-matching extension), Minnesota (rides on Form M3's automatic 6-month extension), Colorado (rides on Form DR 0106's automatic 6-month extension), Maryland (separate Form 510/511E, full payment required up front), Georgia (rides on Form 700/600S extension, federal extension honored under O.C.G.A. sect 48-7-57), Arizona (rides on Form 120/165EXT), Ohio (rides on the federal extension, copy must be attached to Form IT 4738). Explicitly disclosed as a partial survey - over 30 states have enacted a PTET and are not all covered.
- iowa-school-district-surtax-extension.html: Iowa school district and EMS surtax have no separate return or extension - computed as a percentage of state tax on IA 1040 line 19 and added to total state tax and local surtax on line 20, covered by Iowa's own automatic 6-month extension if 90% of total tax (including the surtax) is paid by the original due date. Verified against the 2025 IA 1040.
- oregon-transit-self-employment-tax-extension.html: TriMet and Lane Transit District self-employment tax, reported on Form OR-TM, has no separate extension form - a federal extension or an Oregon individual income tax return extension automatically extends Form OR-TM (check the box on the return). Payment is still due by the original due date regardless; a 20% late-filing penalty applies if filed more than 3 months after the due date including extensions. Verified against the 2025 Form OR-TM Instructions.
- alabama-municipal-occupational-tax-extension.html: Alabama has no statewide statute governing municipal occupational tax extensions - roughly 15-20 cities each impose their own under their own ordinance. Birmingham confirmed this session: the Director of Finance may grant a discretionary extension for reasonable cause, capped at 30 days, with interest and penalty still accruing during the extension (Occupational Tax Code, Ordinance No. 97-184, Section 6). Other Alabama municipalities are explicitly disclosed as not independently checked this session.
- other-extensions.html: Federal payroll tax (Forms 941, 940) has no extension mechanism, only a 10-day filing accommodation for on-time depositors. State unemployment insurance (SUI/SUTA) quarterly reports - all 50 states plus DC addressed against primary sources, every one resolved with a cited answer. Confirmed good-cause extension exceptions: Arkansas (up to 30 days, Regulation No. 6), Idaho (up to 60 days), Missouri (up to 3 months, 8 CSR 10-4.030), New Hampshire (30 days on a $50 fee, RSA 282-A:142), New Mexico (up to 30 days, 11.3.400.410 NMAC - reached via the state's official register archive and cross-checked against two secondary sources after the dws.nm.gov domain rejected every direct fetch), and Washington (good cause, deposit required, WAC 192-310-030(11)). Narrow non-general exceptions: Connecticut (15 extra days, reimbursing employers only), Tennessee and South Carolina (each a payment extension only, not filing). MI had only a 2026 one-time technical waiver, not a standing right; NC's was disaster-specific relief. The rest show no general extension mechanism. FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) gets an automatic extension to October 15, separate from Form 4868.
- master-extension-matrix.html: Flagship sortable table of every jurisdiction and tax type. Federal, all 50 states + DC, Puerto Rico, 8 city/local jurisdictions, state estate/inheritance tax, federal excise, sales/use tax survey, payroll tax, and FBAR all live.
- faq.html: Common extension questions answered.
- disclaimer.html: Site disclaimer and terms.
